arxiv-2104-14261.title: Quantum Computing Platforms: Assessing the Impact on Quality Attributes and SDLC Activities
arxiv-2104-14261.creator: Anonymous, Balwinder Sodhi, Ritu Kapur
arxiv-2104-14261.description: Abstract Practical quantum computing is rapidly becoming a reality. To harness quantum computers’ real potential in software applications, one needs to have an in-depth understanding of all such characteristics of quantum computing platforms (QCPs), relevant from the Software Engineering (SE) perspective.

arxiv-2201-06691.title: Towards a heuristic understanding of the storage effect
arxiv-2201-06691.creator: Evan C. Johnson, Alan Hastings
arxiv-2201-06691.description: Abstract Abstract The storage effect is a general explanation for coexistence in a variable environment. The generality of the storage effect is both a strength — it can be quantified in many systems — and a challenge — there is not a clear relationship between the abstract conditions for storage effect and species’ life-history traits (e.g.

arxiv-2206-15357.title: Supersymmetric Spectral Form Factor and Euclidean Black Holes
arxiv-2206-15357.creator: Sunjin Choi, Seok Kim, Jaewon Song
arxiv-2206-15357.description: Abstract The late-time behavior of spectral form factor (SFF) encodes the inherent discreteness of a quantum system, which should be generically non-vanishing. We study an index analog of the microcanonical spectrum form factor in four-dimensional 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 super Yang-Mills theory.

arxiv-2208-08142.title: Dark states with electromagnetic form factors at electron colliders
arxiv-2208-08142.creator: Yu Zhang, Mao Song, Liangwen Chen
arxiv-2208-08142.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yu Zhang, Mao Song, Liangwen Chen. Electromagnetically neutral dark sector particles may feebly interact with photons through higher dimensional effective operators, such as mass-dimension 5 magnetic and electric dipole moment, and a mass- dimension 6 anapole moment and charge radius operators. In this work, we use hypercharge gauge field form factors to treat dark states, which will induce not only electromagnetic form factors but also the corresponding Z Z boson operators.

arxiv-2302-03423.title: Extreme multistability in symmetrically coupled clocks
arxiv-2302-03423.creator: Zhen Su, Jürgen Kurths, Yaru Liu*, Serhiy Yanchuk
arxiv-2302-03423.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zhen Su, Jürgen Kurths, Yaru Liu*, Serhiy Yanchuk. Extreme multistability (EM) is characterized by the emergence of infinitely many coexisting attractors or continuous families of stable states in dynamical systems. EM implies complex and hardly predictable asymptotic dynamical behavior. We analyse a model for pendulum clocks coupled by springs and suspended on an oscillating base, and show how EM can be induced in this system by a specifically designed coupling. First, we uncover that symmetric coupling can increase the dynamical complexity.

arxiv-2307-07844.title: Studying QGP transport properties in a concurrent minijet+hydro framework
arxiv-2307-07844.creator: Mayank Singh
arxiv-2307-07844.description: Abstract Minijets are ubiquitous in heavy-ion collision experiments. However, they are often excluded from the hydrodynamic simulations of QGP as they do not thermalize at short time scales and are not treated as part of the collective medium. Using a concurrent jet+hydro framework, we show that the minijets could account for a significant portion of particle multiplicity.

arxiv-2401-08435.title: Quantization as a Categorical Equivalence
arxiv-2401-08435.creator: Benjamin H. Feintzeig bfeintze@uw.edu
arxiv-2401-08435.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Benjamin H. Feintzeig bfeintze@uw.edu. We demonstrate that, in certain cases, quantization and the classical limit provide functors that are “almost inverse” to each other. These functors map between categories of algebraic structures for classical and quantum physics, establishing a categorical equivalence. 1
Introduction

The purpose of this paper is to develop tools for assessing the extent to which mathematical models of classical and quantum physics share common structure. To do this, we analyze functors between categories of classical and quantum models.

arxiv-2402-14987.title: On the Performance of Empirical Risk Minimization with Smoothed Data
arxiv-2402-14987.creator: Adam Block, Alexander Rakhlin, Abhishek Shetty
arxiv-2402-14987.description: Abstract In order to circumvent statistical and computational hardness results in sequential decision-making, recent work has considered smoothed online learning, where the distribution of data at each time is assumed to have bounded likeliehood ratio with respect to a base measure when conditioned on the history.

arxiv-2406-10495.title: Segregation Kinetics of Miktoarm Star Polymers: A Dissipative Particle Dynamics Study
arxiv-2406-10495.creator: Dorothy Gogoi, Avinash Chauhan, Sanjay Puri, Awaneesh Singh
arxiv-2406-10495.description: Abstract We study the phase separation kinetics of miktoarm star polymer (MSP) melts and blends with diverse architectures using dissipative particle dynamics simulations. Our study focuses on symmetric and asymmetric miktoarm star polymer (SMSP/AMSP) mixtures based on arm composition and number.

arxiv-2505-05288.title: PlaceIt3D : Language-Guided Object Placement in Real 3D Scenes
arxiv-2505-05288.creator: Ahmed Abdelreheem, Filippo Aleotti, Jamie Watson, Zawar Qureshi, Abdelrahman Eldesokey, Peter Wonka, Gabriel Brostow, Sara Vicente, Guillermo Garcia-Hernando
arxiv-2505-05288.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ahmed Abdelreheem, Filippo Aleotti, Jamie Watson, Zawar Qureshi, Abdelrahman Eldesokey, Peter Wonka, Gabriel Brostow, Sara Vicente, Guillermo Garcia-Hernando. We introduce the task of Language‑Guided Object Placement in Real 3D Scenes. Given a 3D reconstructed point‑cloud scene, a 3D asset, and a natural‑language instruction, the goal is to place the asset so that the instruction is satisfied.

arxiv-2511-02062.title: Yuting Yang
arxiv-2511-02062.description: Abstract There is growing interest in deploying ML inference and knowledge retrieval as services that could support both interactive queries by end users and more demanding request flows that arise from AIs integrated into a end-user applications and deployed as agents. Our central premise is that these latter cases will bring service level latency objectives (SLOs).

pmc-10522873.title: The mineralocorticoid receptor and extra-synaptic NMDA receptor in the lateral habenula involve in the vulnerability to early life stress in the maternal separation model
pmc-10522873.creator: Miseon Kang, Jun-mo Chung, Jihyun Noh, Jeongyeon Kim
pmc-10522873.description: The lateral habenula (LHb) plays a pivotal role in regulating emotional responses during stress reactions, and its hyperactivity has been associated with depression. Recently it has been demonstrated that chronic early-life stress results in individual differences in stress vulnerability among rodents. However, how synaptic function in the LHb varies between susceptibility and resilience to early life stress remains elusive.

pmc-10641156.title: Current and future trends in acute ischemic stroke treatment: direct-to-angiography suite, middle vessel occlusion, large core, and minor strokes
pmc-10641156.creator: Răzvan Alexandru Radu, Gregory Gascou, Paolo Machi, Carolina Capirossi, Vincent Costalat, Federico Cagnazzo
pmc-10641156.description: Since the publication of the landmark thrombectomy trials in 2015, the field of endovascular therapy for ischemic stroke has been rapidly growing. The very low number needed to treat to provide functional benefits shown by the initial randomized trials has led clinicians and investigators to seek to translate the benefits of endovascular therapy to other patient subgroups.

pmc-10684335.title: Interval post-colonoscopy colorectal cancer following a negative colonoscopy in a fecal immunochemical test-based screening program
pmc-10684335.creator: Hilliene J. van de Schootbrugge-Vandermeer, Arthur I. Kooyker, Pieter H. A. Wisse, Iris D. Nagtegaal, Hiltje A. Geuzinge, Esther Toes-Zoutendijk, Lucie de Jonge, Emilie C. H. Breekveldt, Anneke J. van Vuuren, Folkert J. van Kemenade, Christian R. B. Ramakers, Evelien Dekker, Iris Lansdorp-Vogelaar,
pmc-10684335.description: Background In the Dutch colorectal (CRC) screening program, fecal immunochemical test (FIT)-positive individuals are referred for colonoscopy. If no relevant findings are detected at colonoscopy, individuals are reinvited for FIT screening after 10 years. We aimed to assess CRC risk after a negative colonoscopy in FIT-positive individuals.

pmc-10793372.title: Straatsma Syndrome and cataract: case report and review of the literature
pmc-10793372.creator: Casado-Pelaez Blanca, Pascual-Camps Isabel, Inat-Moreno Sergio, Congost-Laguna Candela, Barranco-Gonzalez Honorio, España-Gregori Enrique
pmc-10793372.description: Straatsma Syndrome is known as unilateral myopia, amblyopia, and myelinated retinal nerve fibers (MRNF). The syndrome can be associated with other findings such as nystagmus, strabismus, and optic nerve hypoplasia among others. However, no cases associated with cataract have been reported.

pmc-11594114.title: Empowering Maternal Choice: Exploring Factors Influencing Early Postpartum Contraceptive Adoption Intention Among Pregnant Women in Northeast Ethiopia
pmc-11594114.creator: Niguss Cherie, Muluemebet Abera Wordofa, Gurmesa Tura Debelew
pmc-11594114.description: Background: Despite progress in access to family planning services in many sub-Saharan African countries in recent decades, advances in early postpartum contraceptive adoption remain low, and the unmet need for early postpartum contraceptives is high. According to the Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey report, early postpartum modern contraceptive method uptake is still unacceptably low in Ethiopia.

pmc-11599320.title: Effect of powder air polishing and ultrasonic scaling on the marginal and internal interface (tooth-veneer) of ceramic veneers: an in vitro study
pmc-11599320.creator: Florian Fuchs, Laura Antonia Mayer, Lena Unterschütz, Dirk Ziebolz, Nadia Oberueck, Ellen Schulz‑Kornas, Sebastian Hahnel, Andreas Koenig
pmc-11599320.description: ObjectivesThis study investigated the influence of prophylactic treatments and thermocycling on the marginal and internal veneering interface (tooth-veneer) as well as on the surface texture of ceramic veneers.Materials and methodsA total of 32 extracted human premolars were restored with veneers made of lithium disilicate (LDS) or zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (ZLS).

pmc-12386013.title: Interaction Between Vitamin D Metabolism Genetic Variants: Association with Hypovitaminosis D, Rheumatoid Arthritis, and Its Clinical Disease Activity
pmc-12386013.creator: Bertha Campos-López, Melissa Rivera-Escoto, Adolfo I. Ruiz-Ballesteros, Karen Pesqueda-Cendejas, Paulina E. Mora-García, Mónica R. Meza-Meza, Isela Parra-Rojas, José M. Moreno-Ortíz, Eneida Turiján-Espinoza, Juan M. Vargas-Morales, Sergio Cerpa-Cruz, Ulises De la Cruz-Mosso
pmc-12386013.description: Background: Hypovitaminosis D has been associated with worse rheumatoid arthritis (RA) manifestations. Notably, different genetic studies have reported that approximately 65% of hypovitaminosis D can be partially explained using the presence of single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) in key genes involved in its metabolism.

pmc-12652367.title: STR-Uggles: Overcoming Humic Acid Inhibition Using Combined STR & qPCR Kit Chemistries
pmc-12652367.creator: Caitlin McDonald, Duncan Taylor, Adrian Linacre, Simone Grassi
pmc-12652367.description: Background/Objectives: DNA profiling can fail, or produce poor results, when naturally occurring materials are present during the amplification step. This study demonstrates that simple modifications to the reaction setup can overcome this obstacle. PCR inhibition is caused by a range of compounds including haem, humic acid and dyes.

pmc-12978458.title: Long non-coding RNA PSMB8-AS1 as a potential biomarker for postoperative recurrence in patients with Fuhrman grades 1–3 clear cell renal cell carcinoma
pmc-12978458.creator: Chieko Baba, Hiroshi Hirata, Koichiro Hiyoshi, Takanori Tokunaga, Nakanori Fujii, Kosuke Shimizu, Keita Kobayashi, Takahide Hayano, Yoshiyuki Asai, Koji Shiraishi, Mahbub Hasan, Mahbub Hasan, Mahbub Hasan
pmc-12978458.description: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are important regulators of oncogenesis. In this study, we investigated the tumor-promoting role and prognostic value of the lncRNA PSMB8-AS1 in renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Using lncRNA microarray analysis, we identified PSMB8-AS1 as a candidate gene associated with disease progression and immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance.

pmc-13109644.title: Correlation between heart rate variability and estradiol, progesterone, and the estradiol/progesterone ratio across menstrual phases in healthy women
pmc-13109644.creator: Tara R Salih, Darya S Abdulateef
pmc-13109644.description: Heart rate variability (HRV) is widely used to assess cardiac health, yet uncertainty persists regarding HRV variations across the menstrual cycle and their association with reproductive hormones. Few studies have evaluated the full spectrum of HRV parameters, and most estimated menstrual phases from the last menstrual period without considering individual cycle length.

pmc-13135001.title: Geographical Inequalities in Mortality by Age and Gender in Italy, 2002–2019: Insights from a Spatial Extension of the Lee-Carter Model
pmc-13135001.creator: Francesca Fiori, Andrea Riebler, Sara Martino
pmc-13135001.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Italy reports some of the lowest levels of mortality in the developed world. Recent evidence, however, suggests that even in low-mortality countries improvements may be slowing and regional inequalities widening. This study contributes new empirical evidence to the debate by analysing mortality data by single year of age for males and females across 107 provinces in Italy from 2002 to 2019. We extend the widely used Lee–Carter model to include spatially varying age-specific effects, and further specify it to capture space–age–time interactions.

pmc-13187206.title: Toward trustworthy chatbots: a protocol for red teaming for health related conversations
pmc-13187206.creator: Syed-Amad Hussain, Daniel I Jackson, Ashley Lewis, Eric Fosler-Lussier, Emre Sezgin
pmc-13187206.description: Health-related chatbots require safety assurance beyond factual correctness. We propose a red-teaming protocol for patient-facing AI structured around three pillars: error stratification, dual-pronged testing, and vulnerability-informed mitigation. We distinguish Document Adherence (DA) from Instruction Adherence (IA), deploying adversarial “attacks” across both single-turn and multi-turn exchanges to provoke system failures.

pmc-13373940.title: Behind the Mask: Risk Profiles of Depression and Anxiety in Anesthesiology Residents
pmc-13373940.creator: Diana Guízar-Sánchez, Ana Fresán, Ricardo-Arturo Saracco-Alvarez, María Yoldi-Negrete, Rebeca Robles-García, Carlos-Alfonso Tovilla-Zárate, Chandra Bose
pmc-13373940.description: IntroductionAnesthesiology residents play a crucial role in healthcare, yet the demanding nature of their residency—long hours, high stress, and challenging work conditions—often leads to mental health issues like depression and anxiety. Despite the importance of resident well‐being, mental health problems among anesthesiology residents in Mexico remain underexplored.
